findings.title: Wallet snapshots still break host getters that read private class fields
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Supported generic wallet results still become unusable; complete this public API remedy before release.
findings.reproduction: Return a WalletMatch-compatible class with matched:true, path:'m', private #derived and public get derived() returning it. Read derived after askWallet, then repeat through the actual WordCandidateSearch result.
findings.expected: The returned generic result retains readable supported host fields. Common checked fields remain one-read snapshots.
findings.observed: Common getters and ordinary derived fields work. A private-field getter throws 'Cannot read private member #derived from an object whose class did not declare it' both directly and from the word-search result.
findings.impact: Object.create(given, captured fields) changes the getter receiver to a new object without the original class's private-field brand. A legitimate library/browser host can receive an unusable successful result. Built-in plain-object CLI answers were not shown to fail; no wrong-wallet approval or secret disclosure is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Preserve host result data with the original getter receiver, while retaining immutable one-read matched/path/warning values. Do not use a brandless prototype wrapper as if it were the original generic class instance.
findings.requiredVerification: Private-field-backed derived getter through askWallet and actual word-search output; ordinary own fields, prototype/non-enumerable fields, changing getters and malformed matched controls. Keep cancellation and cleanup regressions.
findings.disposition: The original prototype-getter cases are fixed; the same generic result ownership root cause remains partly fixed.

remediationUpdate.change: Common fields are immutable one-read snapshots. Extra data remains own data; getters, setters and methods keep the original receiver, including private fields, without eager extra getter evaluation.

findings.title: General remediation check records do not identify the exercised source
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Retained log outcomes are intact and fresh targeted checks bind current code; this gap limits attribution of the earlier broader checks.
findings.reproduction: Read the 12 general check records cited by the addendum, or run evidence-check.py. They contain command, UTC times, exit code and log hash, but no sourceBefore/sourceAfter, cwd/environment or retained wrapper identity.
findings.expected: Checks attributed to a fix snapshot identify the exact source/artifact bytes and execution context they exercised, as required by the canonical audit procedure.
findings.observed: All 13 cited logs match their hashes. The residual probe binds c430… explicitly; the other 12 checks lack that binding. A later snapshot does not independently establish which bytes those preceding tests ran against.
findings.impact: The claimed broader passing outcomes are retained, but cannot all be independently assigned to the c430… fix snapshot. This is an evidence attribution limit, not proof that the tests failed or did not run.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a recorder with per-command source identities, working directory, environment and wrapper hashes for future checks. Preserve earlier logs and their limitation; do not invent missing historic bindings or rerun full suites merely to rewrite history.
findings.requiredVerification: Future necessary check records bind unchanged before/after source manifests and tested artifacts, with original logs and exact commands retained.

remediationUpdate.change: Earlier broad logs are explicitly retained as source-unbound historical outcomes, not reattributed to the new fix. Current necessary checks retain exact source/context identities; new addendum validation removes no assertions, and a separate checksum list covers the earlier remediation pairs.

informationalReview: The old probe's two transport failures are instrumentation limits, not surviving decoded-buffer leaks. Constructor capture observes actual allocated arrays and all are wiped in the corrected new probe.

allWiped([]) returns true in the ordinary helper; add a positive allocation-count assertion to keep future cleanup tests from passing vacuously. Current allocation/wipe behavior was independently confirmed.

The retained historical validator does not validate the new addendum; successful modified validation and its skipped assertions were not recorded. Old source/status/artifact mismatches are expected historical identities, not a defect by themselves.

The 51 checksum entries are valid relative to AUD-016-evidence/, not the remediation subfolder. Their verification cwd is undocumented and the 12 remediation pairs are omitted; no wrong parent-directory digest or lost log was found.
Own host fields remain readable but become inherited; JSON/own-property enumeration drops derived. Recorded as a compatibility observation because no separate serialization contract was established.

List publication stops correctly, though the aborting callback is followed by the remaining fingerprint callbacks (eight calls in this fixture). Earlier per-await checks could reduce unnecessary work; no additional publication failure was found.

verificationSummary.meaning: Ordinary regressions are distinct from diagnostic probe checks. No broad suite count from the remediation author is added.
verificationSummary.remaining: AUD-016-API001 is partly fixed; private-field-backed generic host getters still fail. Earlier general-check source attribution is incomplete.
verificationSummary.retainedFailures: edges-expanded initially constructed a double-prefixed metadata fixture and failed at the UR framing guard.
